weeks.read: No clear regime on the week: every axis flat on Atom FX's thresholds; today commodities up, gold down. Mood risk-off 34, the trend sliding from risk-on 57. Strongest this week CAD, AUD, NZD; weakest EUR and CHF. The Fed decides next week (a hold expected, December hike odds rising); the BoJ meets with Japan's core CPI above target at 2.1%; RBA and BoC hike bets; oil at a 22-week high near $103 on Gulf attacks; the US may lift 50% tariffs on some Canadian goods; the euro weighed by France's spread risk and a PMI miss; UK retail sales weak; gold below $4,000, down 4% on the week. US midterms on 3 November.

calls.why: Weakest against strongest, at the 60-day low, on two different stories: France and the PMI miss for the euro, RBA hike bets and commodities for the Aussie. A cross, so the Fed matters less.
Oil at $103, BoC hike bets, the tariff relief; the week broke below its 20-day range (low 1.3964). Risk: a hawkish Fed lifting the dollar.
At the 60-day low and falling a week; the euro weak, the yen bid as a haven and ahead of a BoJ with inflation above target. Risk: a dovish BoJ.
The franc is the second weakest this week even with markets uneasy, and the dollar keeps its yield advantage (10Y 4.99%) into a hawkish-hold Fed. Risk: a real risk-off rush into havens.
Below $4,000 intraday, down 4% on the week, higher US yields and December hike odds. Risk: the midterms and any shock bring the haven back.
Strong against weak without the dollar: RBA bets against a franc that is not acting as a haven. Overlaps the EURAUD call in spirit; kept to test whether the franc's weakness is real.
